sample_data.method: Embedded directly in source as a hardcoded JS array (SEED_MEDS, in index.html), reshaped from the organisers' published P02 fixture, case PUB-12 (its 'today' matches this build's date). A plain-JSON copy of the same 44 items is kept at data/stock.json for inspection.
sample_data.reset_instructions: The sample dataset itself is static and never mutated on disk, so reloading index.html always starts from the same 44 items. Only user actions during a session (Mark returned, Quick add) are persisted, and only in that browser's localStorage under the key 'pharmacy-shelf-check-v1'. To restore the original state for judging: open the page in a new private/incognito window, or open DevTools > Application (Storage in Firefox) > Local Storage > the page's origin > delete the 'pharmacy-shelf-check-v1' key, then reload.

problem_solving_method: Read the problem statement and the three published rulings (R-27, R-04, R-24) first to fix the exact bucket definitions and value formula before writing code. Took the organisers' own published P02 sample-data fixture and used case PUB-12 (its 'today' field equals this build's actual date), reshaping it into the app's schema instead of inventing numbers. Independently hand-computed bucket counts and BDT totals from that same fixture in a separate Python script to check the app's output matched exactly. Built the whole thing as one dependency-free HTML/CSS/JS file with no framework and no backend, so the four groups recompute live from the real current date rather than being pre-labelled in the data, per the 'must be worked out from today's date' constraint. Chose a static client-side app over a backend+database because the brief is one pharmacist looking at one screen — that meets the requirement with the fewest moving parts, at the cost of the limitations listed below.

R1.evidence: index.html: SEED_MEDS array (44 medicines with name/batch/company/quantity/unit_price_bdt/expiry_date), mirrored at data/stock.json. 10 already expired, 6 expiring <=30d, 8 expiring <=90d, 17 safe (several >1 year out).

R2.evidence: index.html: bucketOf() computes Expired/Expiring<=30d/Expiring<=90d/Safe from new Date() on every render (never pre-labelled in data); renderStats() writes the four live counts into #countExpired, #countSoon30, #countMid90, #countSafe, each also usable as a table filter.

R3.evidence: index.html: markReturned() sets returned:true + returnedDate and re-renders; renderTable() excludes returned items from the active list, renderReturned() lists them separately under 'Returned to distributor' with an Undo action. renderStats()/getFiltered() filter on !m.returned before any bucketing or summing (ruling R-24).

R4.evidence: index.html: renderStats() computes heroExpiredValue and heroSoonValue as sum(quantity * unit_price_bdt) over the Expired group and the Expiring<=30d group respectively (ruling R-27), with 'expiring soon' scoped to 0-30 days inclusive and kept separate from expired (ruling R-04).

major_design_decisions: Mutually-exclusive buckets (Expired / <=30d / <=90d / Safe) computed live from the real current date, never pre-labelled in the data, so the four tile counts always sum to the active item count and stay correct on any day the page is opened.
Sample data sourced from the organisers' own published P02 fixture (case PUB-12) rather than invented numbers, reshaped into the app's field names.
No backend: 'Mark returned' and 'Quick add' state is kept in the browser's localStorage, matching the brief's single-pharmacist single-screen scope.

Status and accent colors were run through a colorblind-simulation + WCAG-contrast validator (OKLCH lightness band, chroma floor, CVD Delta-E separation) for both light and dark mode rather than picked by eye.
known_limitations: Single-browser state: returns and quick-adds live in that browser's localStorage, not a shared database — two devices won't see each other's changes.
No authentication/authorization — anyone with the URL can mark items returned or add stock.
Only a single 'returned on' date is kept per item; no broader edit/audit history beyond the one-click Undo in the Returned list.
The 6-month chart is forward-looking only (skips already-expired stock by design) and reflects state at render time.

ai_tools_used.used_for: Full build: reading the spec and rulings, selecting and reshaping the official sample fixture, writing all dashboard logic (bucketing, value-at-risk, returns, search/filter, chart, quick-add) and UI/CSS, and drafting this documentation.
ai_tools_used.how_output_was_verified: Bucket counts and BDT totals were independently recomputed from the same source fixture in a standalone Python script and cross-checked against the running page's output; the page was exercised headlessly with Playwright to confirm search, bucket filtering, mark-returned, and quick-add all behave correctly and update totals live; the status/accent color palette was checked with a colorblind-simulation and WCAG-contrast validator script rather than eyeballed.
